If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over last 5 days, increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to capture bullish momentum.

If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) over last 5 days, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid overestimating downside risk.

If sentiment swings sharply from positive to negative within 3 days, adjust forecast downward by 1–2% in mid-horizon (8–15 days) to reflect sentiment reversal.

If sentiment remains neutral (0.33–0.67) over last 5 days, apply no correction to forecast in early horizon, but reduce by 0.5–1% in late horizon (16–30 days) to account for mean reversion.

If sentiment is positive but price has recently broken above 70, increase forecast by 1–2% in mid-horizon to reflect momentum continuation.

If sentiment is negative but price has recently broken below 65, reduce forecast by 1–2% in mid-horizon to reflect risk of further decline.
